problem: The SSH line is truncated: 'ssh -i key.pem ec2-user@' has no host after the @, so a student who copies it gets an error, and the login name differs by AMI (ec2-user for Amazon Linux, ubuntu for Ubuntu images).
fix: Show the full form: ssh -i key.pem ec2-user@<public-IP-or-public-DNS>, and add one clause that the user name depends on the AMI (ec2-user for Amazon Linux, ubuntu for Ubuntu).

problem: Section 2 says of an EBS volume 'The volume outlives the instance', but the Exam traps correctly say a terminated instance deletes its root volume by default. Read together the two statements contradict each other.
fix: In Section 2 write: an EBS volume is independent of the instance and can be detached and re-attached; it survives termination only if DeleteOnTermination is false, because the root volume is deleted on termination by default.

problem: The figure has no load balancer, yet the caption, Section 3 and step 3 of the worked example all place an Application Load Balancer in the public subnet in front of the web instances. The reader cannot match the diagram to the design.
fix: Add a node such as 'ALB' with note 'port 443, health checks' in the public subnet, with edges internet gateway → ALB and ALB → Web EC2 A / Web EC2 B, and change the caption to say users reach the load balancer on 443.

problem: 'There is no seek' is imprecise. S3 does serve byte-range GET requests (partial reads) over HTTPS; what it does not support is in-place or partial writes to an existing object.
fix: Say: you can read part of an object with an HTTP Range GET, but there is no block-level random access and no way to overwrite part of an object — a write replaces the whole object.

problem: The unsupported claim that 'Most Indian startups, banks and government portals run at least part of their stack this way' invites an examiner question and cannot be backed by the chapter.
fix: Soften to: many Indian startups, banks and government portals rent at least part of their stack this way, paying by the hour or by the gigabyte.
